transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-17 | 15:00 UTC | 52 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Clearstream Head of ML), Ethan Park (Clearstream Dir. Infra), Olivia Chen (Clearstream Procurement)

Auto-generated summary: Quick renewal/expansion check; focus on capacity bump, region add (EU), and governance docs.

[00:00] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Carlos here from Redwood, Priya on the line. Maya, Ethan, Olivia, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Thanks Carlos. We wanted to do a quick cadence check; our Q3 forecast came in higher so we're re-evaluating dedicated options and the EU VPC pilot.
[00:30] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya. Happy to walk through perf numbers and pilot runbook. We ran a dry benchmark last week against a sample trace and saw predictable P50 improvements with dedicated GPU pools.
[00:44] Ethan Park (Clearstream): Quick question on that — when you say "predictable" does that include KV cache warmup? Our traffic is pretty bursty at 09:00 UTC and we see cold-start penalties.
[00:58] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Good call. The benchmarks included prefix caching and KV cache scenarios; the dedicated path benefits from persistent cache across workers so cold starts are less severe. We still recommend a short warmup window to prime the cache during the pilot.
[01:20] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Our primary ask is 350 rps sustained during peak with P50 < 15ms and P95 < 120ms for response generation. Is that in scope for Dedicated?
[01:33] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Yes — on Dedicated we can design for that. Quick caveat: P50 15ms depends on sequence length and model choice; if you're using longer contexts the numbers shift. We should align on model selection and quantization profile.
[01:50] Olivia Chen (Clearstream): From procurement side, we need the contract amendment template and an idea of lead time. We also need compliance artifacts — SOC2, ISO, and KMS notes for data at rest.
[02:05] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): We'll share SOC2 and ISO certs. For KMS we support several integrations; we can map to your HSM provider. I'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[02:18] Ethan Park (Clearstream): Are there any known gotchas with our cloud provider? We're on AZ-Europe-North east and run strict VPC peering rules.
[02:31] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): We support AZ regions. For VPC private control plane the onboarding is manual but we've done similar peering with strict rules — firewall ports, route table exceptions. We'll include a network diagram.
[02:45] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Great. Can we talk about fallback behavior? If Dedicated nodes get saturated, what's the graceful degradation?
[02:55] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Default policy is auto-fallback to a compatible hosted model variant in a different capacity tier. You can also configure canary-fallbacks or queue depth thresholds. We can show logs and tracing to prove requests were served via fallback during the pilot.
[03:12] Ethan Park (Clearstream): Hmm. We prefer predictable cost vs risking cross-tenant hosted failover. Is there an option to reserve burst capacity?
[03:22] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Yes couple options — you can reserve dedicated headroom or enable burst capacity as an add-on. That gets priced differently but keeps traffic on customer-dedicated pools first.
[03:35] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Cost sensitivity is important. We ran an internal model and DeepServe came in slightly cheaper on per-token, but Redwood's latency profile was better in last benchmark.
[03:48] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Totally expected. We'll send a side-by-side cost/latency sheet based on your 350 rps forecast including quantization scenarios. That should help the procurement decision.
[04:02] Olivia Chen (Clearstream): For contract, do you require a minimum term for Dedicated?
[04:09] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Standard is a 12-month reserved commitment for Dedicated tiers, but we can do a 6-month starter with graduated uplift — it's flexible depending on commitment level.
[04:20] Ethan Park (Clearstream): For security, we need audit logs and retention windows. Also, do you provide per-token attribution for cost analysis?
[04:33] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Audit logs are available from the Private control plane, and the Console gives token-level cost breakdowns. Retention is configurable — we'll include the retention policy options in the docs.
[04:46] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Ok, let's outline the pilot. We want a 2-week EU VPC pilot: week 0 (network & IAM), week 1 (benchmarks & traffic run), week 2 (analysis + signoff). Is that realistic?
[05:03] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): That's doable. We'll need your anonymized traffic trace and peak-hour windows to run realistic load tests. Also need a point person for network approvals — Ethan?
[05:15] Ethan Park (Clearstream): Yup, I'll own network. I'll try to get the trace by Thursday.
[05:21] Olivia Chen (Clearstream): From procurement timeline, if pilot signoff is by mid-July we can route the amendment in the next procurement cycle.
[05:31] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Sounds good. We'll aim to get docs out this week so you can review before the pilot.
[05:37] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): One more technical thing — quantization and model variants. We run some heavy reranking and embeddings alongside generation; can Dedicated host mixed workloads without noisy neighbor issues?
[05:50] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Yes, Dedicated gives you control over GPU pools and you can isolate workloads by route. For embeddings we recommend separate node pools or dedicated inference lanes to avoid contention.
[06:05] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Any caveats for on-prem or private deployments? We may need air-gapped for some PHI use cases down the line.
[06:16] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Private on-prem is an option but timeline and ops overhead are higher. For PHI, VPC + customer-managed KMS usually suffices if data residency and audit trails are preserved; on-prem is a later stage.
[06:33] Ethan Park (Clearstream): Ok. Can you quantify expected token-cost delta for quantized int8 vs fp16?
[06:43] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Ballpark: quantization can drop CPU/GPU time 20–40% depending on model. We'll give you a delta in the pricing spreadsheet by scenario — int8, int4, and fp16.
[06:58] Olivia Chen (Clearstream): Back to procurement, who will sign the amendment on Redwood's side? We need the legal contact.
[07:06] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): I'll introduce you to our Contracts lead, Sarah Liu, in the doc thread. She'll handle the amendment and SOW.
[07:16] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Great. Are there any integration playbooks or runbooks you can share to speed the pilot?
[07:23] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Yes, early onboarding runbook, network checklist, and a sample benchmark harness. I'll share links.
[07:33] Ethan Park (Clearstream): If we find we need to shift traffic mid-pilot, how quickly can you scale additional nodes?
[07:41] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Dedicated scaling is configurable — the autoscaler can add nodes within minutes depending on available hardware in-region; provisioning a new geo might take longer. For burst we can pre-authorize capacity.
[07:56] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Let's capture acceptance criteria: 350 rps sustained, P50 < 15ms, P95 < 120ms, successful VPC peering, SOC2 + KMS integration verified, and a contract amendment routed.
[08:12] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Noted. I'll put those as acceptance criteria in the pilot SOW.
[08:20] Olivia Chen (Clearstream): Any other vendors we should be aware of? Our infra team looked at CloudModelX for private deployments but they flagged a longer ops runway.
[08:32] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Understood. We'll include a competitor comparison slide in the packet.
[08:38] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Ok, last question: can we see a recent latency trace from a similar customer in EU (anonymized)?
[08:47] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Yes we can share anonymized graphs — I'll attach one from a retail customer with similar RPS.
[08:55] Ethan Park (Clearstream): I'll follow up with the firewall team for port exceptions and peering.
[09:00] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Thanks, team. Quick recap and next steps: Carlos will send pricing and contract contact; Priya will push SOC2/ISO and the runbook; Ethan to provide trace; Olivia to confirm procurement window. We'll aim to kick pilot week of 6/30.
[09:20] Maya Thompson (Clearstream): Sounds good. Thanks all.
[09:24] Olivia Chen (Clearstream): Thanks.
[09:26] Carlos Mendez (Redwood): Appreciate it. We'll follow up with the doc bundle today.

(Transcript includes normal transcription noise — occasional misheard acronyms e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "k v cash"; names may be slightly off in export.)
